blocks.text: Buying an Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) Farm in Abbotsford

parts.t: Approximately 72% of the City of Abbotsford's land base sits inside British Columbia's Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR), making Abbotsford the highest-grossing agricultural municipality in Canada per hectare. Active farm listings on this page span five distinct farming districts: Sumas Prairie (deep lake-bottom soils suited to dairy, vegetables, turf, poultry, and berries), Matsqui Prairie north to the Fraser River (dairy, forage, and berries), Bradner and Aberdeen on the western bench (blueberries, nurseries, greenhouses, and horse farms), and South Poplar near the US border.

When evaluating an Abbotsford farm, land value is driven by soil capability, drainage and irrigation infrastructure, barn and outbuilding utility, residential footprint, and Highway 1 corridor access. On blueberry and raspberry farms, buyers must inspect variety mix (such as Duke, Draper, Calypso, Bluecrop, or Elliott), plant age, trellis and drip-irrigation condition, and historical pack-out receipts. On livestock and poultry operations, barn engineering, biosecurity layout, environmental farm plan compliance, and marketing-board quota transferability determine commercial value.

blocks.text: ALR Zoning, Floodplain Rules, and Farm Tax Status in Abbotsford

parts.t: Most working farms in Abbotsford are zoned A1 or A2 (Agricultural) under City of Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 and governed by the Agricultural Land Commission Act. Buyers should verify: (1) whether existing houses, farm-help dwellings, processing buildings, and fill placements were completed with municipal permits and ALC approvals; (2) Floodplain Development Permit Area and Flood Construction Level (FCL) rules on Sumas Prairie, Matsqui Prairie, and Glen Valley parcels; (3) water licences or irrigation ditch rights along the Sumas and Matsqui drainage systems; and (4) GST implications and BC Assessment Farm Class income thresholds.

Where are most working farms located in Abbotsford?

Abbotsford farms are concentrated in four main agricultural areas: Sumas Prairie in the east, Matsqui Prairie in the north, Bradner and Glen Valley in the northwest, and Aberdeen and South Poplar in the west and southwest.
What types of farms are most common in Abbotsford?

Abbotsford leads British Columbia in blueberry, raspberry, poultry (broiler, layer, and turkey), dairy, egg, field vegetable, turf, nursery, and greenhouse production, alongside private equestrian acreages.
How much farm income is required to keep BC Assessment Farm Class tax status?

For parcels between 0.8 hectares (1.98 acres) and 4 hectares (10 acres), BC Assessment generally requires $2,500 in annual gross qualifying agricultural sales (reported every two years); for parcels over 4 hectares, the threshold is $2,500 plus 5% of the actual farm land value.
Can I build a second house on an ALR farm in Abbotsford?

Under current ALC and City of Abbotsford rules, parcels in the ALR may qualify for one additional small residence (up to 90 square metres / 968 sq ft) subject to municipal zoning, servicing, and siting setbacks, while larger farm-help accommodation requires an ALC application demonstrating agricultural need.
Is GST charged on the purchase of an Abbotsford farm?

GST generally applies to the commercial farmland and farm outbuildings portion of an ALR sale (while the used residential house and immediate 0.5-hectare curtilage are typically GST-exempt), though GST-registered buyers acquiring a farm for commercial production can often self-assess using a GST election with their accountant.
What floodplain checks apply to farms on Sumas Prairie and Matsqui Prairie?

Both prairies sit inside the City of Abbotsford Floodplain Development Permit Area. Before removing subjects, verify the parcel's ground elevation, Flood Construction Level (FCL) for dwellings and barns, Barrowtown or Matsqui drainage ditch proximity, and property insurance terms.
